issue_context.title: csi-translation-lib: Azure disk type is not properly translated
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

/kind bug
/sig storage
/area provider/azure


#### What happened:

Creation of a PVC that that uses a StorageClass with the in-tree provisioner `kubernetes.io/azure-disk` and parameter `kind: managed` fails.

#### What you expected to happen:
The above to work.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1. Create an Azure cluster with CSI enabled

2. Create StorageClass with the in-tree provisioner `kubernetes.io/azure-disk`

```yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: sc-test
provisioner: kubernetes.io/azure-disk
allowVolumeExpansion: true
parameters:
  storageaccounttype: Premium_LRS
  kind: managed
```

3. Create PVC and Deployment

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: claim
spec:
  storageClassName: sc-test
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 4Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nginx-deployment
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: centos
        command: ["/bin/sh"]
        args: ["-c", "while true; do echo $(date -u) >> /data/out.txt; sleep 5; done"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: persistent-storage
          mountPath: /data
      volumes:
      - name: persistent-storage
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: claim
```

5. Make sure that external-provisioner fails with:

```
E0702 10:16:07.216628       1 volume_store.go:144] error saving volume pv-shoot--foo--bar-01956d9d-bdbf-4602-b1b6-6c1b20a86349: PersistentVolume "pv-shoot--foo--bar-01956d9d-bdbf-4602-b1b6-6c1b20a86349" is invalid: [spec.azureDisk.kind: Unsupported value: "managed": supported values: "Dedicated", "Managed", "Shared", spec.azureDisk.diskURI: Unsupported value: "/subscriptions/<omitted>/resourceGroups/shoot--foo--bar/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/pv-shoot--foo--bar-01956d9d-bdbf-4602-b1b6-6c1b20a86349": supported values: "https://{account-name}.blob.core.windows.net/{container-name}/{disk-name}.vhd"]
```

I see that there is mismatch between the csi-translation lib and the docs in https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azuredisk-csi-driver/blob/v1.4.0/docs/driver-parameters.md. The csi-translation-lib is translating in-tree PV to CSI with uppercase ("Managed"), so this means that the docs (that state allowed values are with lowercase - "managed") are wrong. If we want to support the lowercase values, then the csi-translation logic needs to be adapted.

/cc @andyzhangx
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/103439 would fix this issue, pls use `Managed` kind as a workaround, thanks.
there is a quick fix in azure disk csi driver: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azuredisk-csi-driver/pull/915, it would be merged in v1.5 version

review_comments: Can we make the CSI driver case insensitive?
there is already a fix in CSI driver to make case insensitive
Can something not managed be specified?
since CSI driver only supports managed, we can only support `managed` in csi migration.

> Can we make the CSI driver case insensitive?

In theory, we could fix it in volume validation, while since this issue only exists in csi migration, may be not necessary now
What happens if someone is using a volume that is unmanaged with CSI migration?

> What happens if someone is using a volume that is unmanaged with CSI migration?

it's not supported, volume would be in unattached state forever. unmanaged disk is actually deprecated in Azure, if user still wants to use unmanaged disk, they need to turn off csi migration for disk.

Can a user use unmanaged disks with in-tree driver today? If so, we may need to also send a deprecation notice for this.

Also, should we return an error if the kind is not supported?
already added the error code and depreciation notice in doc notes if kind is not supported.
Thanks, can you also clarify, is there any documentation we can point to users on how to migrate their disks from unmanaged to managed?
